name: The Requirements Sharpener
oneLiner: Rewrites a vague requirement into precise, testable Given/When/Then criteria grounded in the actual design screenshots — additively, never overwriting the original.
lead: Requirements are usually written before the design exists, so they stay fuzzy — 'the user can submit the form' with no real button labels or error messages. This agent feeds the requirement plus the finished design screenshots to a multimodal LLM and gets back sharp criteria that quote the actual on-screen text and cite the screen each came from. The original acceptance criteria are read once and never written back — the sharpened set is stored alongside.
chore: Making a requirement like 'show an error if the input is invalid' testable means cross-referencing it against the design mockups by hand: the exact error wording, the precise button label, which states are disabled, what the empty screen reads — then rewriting each point. It's meticulous, and anything missed becomes a gap a tester hits later.
instead: The agent pulls the requirement, the prior feature briefing, and the exported design package — including the screenshots as base64 image data — and sends them to a multimodal Gemini model that reads the pixels, not just descriptions. It returns Given/When/Then criteria that quote exact labels and messages and cite the source screen, added alongside the untouched original.
whyItMatters: Vague requirements produce vague tests that miss real defects. Grounding every criterion in the actual design closes that gap before the first test is authored.

howItWorks.step: Fetches the requirement — title, description, original acceptance criteria — live from ADO.
howItWorks.explain: A thin read-and-normalize over the raw work item. Both rich-text fields — `System.Description` and `Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria` — are HTML in ADO, so `cleanHtml` flattens them to the plain text a language model can actually reason over, and each field is `|| ''`-guarded so a missing value becomes an empty string rather than `undefined`. This `acceptanceCriteria` is the **original**, captured once here and never written back — the whole agent is additive, storing sharpened criteria alongside it. `parentId` is stringified for uniform handling (empty when there's no parent) and `adoUrl` is retained so downstream output can deep-link each criterion back to its source ticket.

howItWorks.step: Loads the prior feature briefing for this requirement, if present, to reuse its business rules and user flows.
howItWorks.explain: Best-effort enrichment from a prior Test-Scout briefing — its absence must not break the run, so a missing `intelPath` returns a fully-formed `{ found: false, ... }` shape instead of throwing. When a briefing exists, `businessRules` is defensively normalized because entries arrive in mixed shapes: the `.map` coerces a `{description}`, a `{name}`, or a bare string all down to text, `.filter(r => r && r.length > 10)` discards empties and trivially short fragments, and `.slice(0, 10)` caps the count. The caps are prompt-budget controls — 10 rules and an 800-char `summary` — deliberately small so this context grounds the model without crowding out the design screenshots, which are the higher-signal input for this agent.

howItWorks.step: Loads the design package — frame-structure JSON, the on-screen text listing, and the screenshots themselves.
howItWorks.explain: Assembles the multimodal payload with everything guarded and bounded. The text artifacts — frame-structure JSON and the on-screen text listing — are each `existsSync`-gated and hard-capped (`slice(0, 20000)` / `slice(0, 15000)`) so a large export can't blow the token budget, degrading to `''` when absent. Screenshots are loaded only when `includeImages` is set (the `--no-images` flag clears it) and the folder exists; the `.sort()` before `.slice(0, MAX_DESIGN_IMAGES)` makes the selection deterministic — the same 8 files every run, in filename order — rather than filesystem-arbitrary. Each image is `base64`-encoded for inline transport in the Gemini request, and `imageCount` is returned so the final result can honestly report how many screens actually grounded the criteria.

howItWorks.step: Sends the requirement, the briefing, and the design screenshots to a multimodal LLM in one request, asking for sharper criteria.
howItWorks.explain: Hand-builds the Gemini `contents` payload as a single interleaved `parts` array so the model reasons over the real screens, not prose about them. Text goes first, then each image is pushed as an `inlineData` part immediately followed by a `[Design image attached above: <filename>]` text marker — that pairing is what lets the model cite *which* screen a criterion came from, the whole point of this agent. `generationConfig` uses `?? 8192`/`?? 0.2` defaults, the low temperature chosen so the model quotes exact on-screen labels rather than paraphrasing them. Extraction is defensively deep-chained — `data.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.text || ''` — so a safety-blocked or empty response returns an empty string the caller can handle, instead of throwing on an undefined path.

howItWorks.step: Parses back Given/When/Then criteria that quote exact labels and cite the source screen — stored alongside the untouched original.
howItWorks.explain: Assembles the per-story result record, and its ordering encodes the agent's core contract: `originalAC: story.acceptanceCriteria` is stored **verbatim, never overwritten**, and `refinedAC: parsed.refinedAC` sits beside it as an additive layer — the sharpened criteria never replace the source. Every field is parsed off `parseLLMJson(llm.answer)` rather than raw `JSON.parse`, and `parsed.summary || ''` defaults the optional summary so the record shape is uniform whether or not the model returned one. The record also carries provenance — `screenshotsUsed: figma.imageCount`, `intelligenceUsed`, `llmModel`, `llmTimeMs` — so each output is auditable: you can see exactly how many screens and which model produced these criteria, and `error: ''` marks a clean run in the results array.
howItWorks.code:
const parsed = parseLLMJson(llm.answer); // tolerant parse of the model JSON before we trust any field off it
results.push({
  storyId, title: story.title, state: story.state, adoUrl: story.adoUrl,
  feature,
  originalAC: story.acceptanceCriteria,   // preserved verbatim, never overwritten
  refinedAC: parsed.refinedAC,             // additive — cites design + intelligence sources
  summary: parsed.summary || '', // summary is optional in the response — default to empty so the record shape stays stable
  llmModel: llm.model, llmTimeMs: llm.timeMs,
  screenshotsUsed: figma.imageCount, // provenance: how many screens actually informed these criteria
  intelligenceUsed: true, error: '',
});

howItWorks.step: Serializes the result to JSON, Markdown, a Word document, and an import-ready xlsx with one row per criterion.
howItWorks.explain: Flattens the nested result set into the exact grain ADO's import expects: the outer loop walks `results`, the inner loop walks each story's `refinedAC`, and `ws.addRow` emits **one row per criterion** — not per story — so a story with five sharpened criteria becomes five importable rows. The column set (`storyId`, `acId`, Given/When/Then, `designs`) mirrors an ADO paste-back layout, and `designs: (ac.designReferences || []).join('\n')` collapses each criterion's source-screen citations into one newline-separated cell, with the `|| []` guard so a criterion that cited nothing still writes cleanly. The file is timestamped like every other output, so each run is a distinct snapshot ready to paste straight back into the tool.

examples.caption: A fuzzy 'submit the form' requirement
examples.input: A requirement reading 'The user can submit feedback', plus a design folder with the feedback screen's empty, error, and success states.
examples.output: Sharpened criteria such as 'Given the feedback box is empty, When the user taps Send, Then the Send button stays disabled and the hint reads "Please enter feedback to continue"' — quoting the exact text from `02_error.png`, appended below the untouched original.

examples.caption: A character-limit rule from the briefing
examples.input: A requirement with no length rule, but a prior briefing noting 'feedback is capped at 500 characters'.
examples.output: A criterion fusing design and briefing: 'Given the user has typed 500 characters, When they type one more, Then input is blocked and a counter shows 500/500' — citing both the design screen and the briefing's business rule.

underHood.heading: Fetches the story
underHood.whenRuns: First, when the agent starts on a story.
underHood.output: Its title, description, and original acceptance criteria, via the ADO REST API.

underHood.heading: Checks for a prior briefing
underHood.output: Any test-intelligence summary — business rules, user-flow steps — found in prior feature folders; proceeds without one under `--allow-no-intelligence`.

underHood.heading: Loads the design package
underHood.input: A folder of exported design files.
underHood.output: The frame structure, every on-screen text string, and up to 8 screenshots as base64 image data.

underHood.heading: Queries the multimodal LLM
underHood.input: The story, the briefing summary, and the design text and screenshots in one request.
underHood.output: Given/When/Then criteria quoting exact button labels and error text and citing the source screen, via Gemini 2.0 Flash reading the images directly.

underHood.heading: Keeps the original untouched
underHood.output: The sharpened criteria stored alongside — never replacing — the story's `originalAC`.

underHood.heading: Writes the outputs
underHood.output: JSON, Markdown, a one-row-per-criterion xlsx ready to import into ADO, and a Word document with `--word`.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Read access to Azure DevOps and a **personal access token** (`ADO_PAT`).
A Google Gemini API key — this agent needs a multimodal model, since it sends the design screenshots directly.
A folder of exported design files (frame-structure JSON, a text listing, and the screenshots).
Ideally a prior feature briefing from the Test Scout — the agent runs without one under `--allow-no-intelligence`.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime for the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program executed under Node. One-time install per machine.
steps.firstRun: First time on a new machine only.

steps.label: Clone the code and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` resolves the agent's dependencies — the ADO REST client, the xlsx/docx writers, and the Gemini client — into `node_modules`.
steps.rerun: No-op unless the dependency set changed.

steps.label: Set the environment variables.
steps.why: Read at startup — the PAT to fetch the story, the Gemini key for the multimodal call that reads the requirement and the design screenshots together and writes sharper criteria.

steps.label: Point it at the requirement and its design folder — dry-run first.
steps.why: `--story-ids` is the requirement ticket number(s); `--figma-dir` is the exported design folder. `--dry-run` fetches everything and confirms the story and designs resolved, without an LLM call.
steps.firstRun: Fetches the story, checks for a prior briefing and usable design files, and skips the LLM step.

steps.label: Run for real.
steps.why: Drop `--dry-run`. Sends the requirement, the prior briefing (if found), and the screenshots to the multimodal model and gets back sharper Given/When/Then criteria. `--word` also writes a docx.
steps.firstRun: Generates the sharpened criteria and writes every output.
steps.rerun: No change-tracking — recomputes fresh from the current requirement text and designs; re-run whenever the design updates.

steps.label: If there's no prior briefing, allow the agent to proceed without one.
steps.why: By default the agent requires a prior feature briefing (from the Test Scout) for its business rules. This flag proceeds on the requirement text and designs alone.

steps.label: Open the sharpened criteria.
steps.why: Outputs land as JSON, Markdown, an import-ready xlsx (one row per criterion), and — with --word — a docx. The original requirement wording is always preserved alongside, never overwritten.

inputs.name: --story-ids <ids>
inputs.desc: Comma-separated requirement ticket number(s) to sharpen.

inputs.name: --figma-dir <path>
inputs.desc: A folder of exported design files — frame-structure JSON, on-screen text listing, and screenshots.

inputs.name: --word / --dry-run / --no-images / --allow-no-intelligence
inputs.desc: --word adds a docx; --dry-run skips the LLM call; --no-images sends text only (no screenshots); --allow-no-intelligence proceeds without a prior briefing.

outputs.name: StoryAC_Refinement_<timestamp>.json / .md
outputs.desc: Every requirement's original criteria alongside the sharpened Given/When/Then criteria, each citing the source screen and label.

outputs.name: StoryAC_Refinement_<timestamp>.xlsx
outputs.desc: One row per sharpened criterion — Story ID, Given, When, Then, Design Refs — ready to paste back into ADO.

runbook.rerun: No change-tracking — every run re-reads the requirement and design folder fresh. Re-run whenever the design changes (a new screenshot, an updated label) or the requirement's wording is edited; the original text is never overwritten, so nothing is lost by re-running.
runbook.integrate: Feed it the briefing from the **Test Scout** for richer, rule-aware criteria. Its sharpened output is the ideal input to the **Test-Plan Author** — precise Given/When/Then criteria yield far more accurate drafted test cases than a vague one-line requirement.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: pass a vague requirement and its design folder, and watch precise, screenshot-grounded criteria come back.
script: Open a terminal; have the design screenshots open in a viewer for comparison.
Say: 'This agent looks at the actual screens and rewrites a vague requirement into something exact.'
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; one line on what Node is.
Run `npm install` (or note it's done); explain it grabs the helper libraries.
Show the `export` lines including the AI key; say this is the only client-specific part.
Run the command with `--dry-run`; show it confirming the story and the design folder were both found.
Re-run without `--dry-run`, adding `--word`; narrate as it sends the text and screenshots together to the AI.
Open the Markdown output; show the original requirement wording untouched at the top.
Scroll to the sharpened criteria; read one that quotes an exact button label and cites the screen it came from.
Close: 'Nothing was guessed — every sharpened line points back to a real pixel on a real screen.'
